These are detector_definitions rows as 0008_risk.sql declares the table, one per detector M07 section 3.2 names, and EVERY VALUE IN parameters CARRIES THE LINE OF M07 IT WAS READ FROM. provenance._note: The authority is a document in this repository rather than a retrieved publication, so there is no artifact to commit and no `artifact_sha256`. What replaces both is the LINE-LEVEL CITE on every value plus `authority_sha256`, the digest of the authority file as read. A cite that still resolves against a DIFFERENT M07 is a cite that has silently changed meaning; the digest is what turns that from an archaeology exercise into a one-line check. `generate.mjs` re-derives it and refuses a disagreement.

row_defaults._note: THREE COLUMNS OF `detector_definitions` ARE `NOT NULL` AND M07 GIVES NO VALUE FOR TWO OF THEM. They are declared here, once, rather than repeated eighteen times, and each says plainly whether it is transcribed or CHOSEN. A chosen value is not a cited value and this file does not let the two wear the same clothes: `generate.mjs` requires `state: "chosen"` to carry a `reason` and refuses a `cite` on it, because a citation attached to a choice is the exact defect this whole file exists to prevent.

It is recorded as a finding in the pull-request body. The column is part of the primary key, so it cannot be null and the choice cannot be deferred; what it can be is LABELLED, which is what this block does. A later tuning supersedes a row by `effective_to` and a new `version` under SD-M7-03, so nothing here forecloses the founder's own scheme.
